# Starkiller (HP_Legend) vs Qui-Gon Jinn (Meatpants)

- Directory section: Miscellaneous
- Directory line: Forum Debate, May 27-July 17, 2020 | Victor: HP_Legend (Judge Decision 2:0)
- Thread: https://www.suspectinsightforums.com/t3352-ss-starkiller-arkhamasylum3-vs-qui-gon-jinn-meatpants
- Raw full-thread text (all pages): raw/threads/082.txt
- Notes compiled: 2026-10-20

## Matchup & conditions
- **Starkiller** (TFU II), argued by HP_Legend (posting as NotAA3/"Guest"), vs **Qui-Gon Jinn** (TPM), argued by Meatpants ("MP"). Legends, standard rules.
- Holocron canon policy (as of Sept 2012) governs source validity (MP, P6).
- Thread length: 46 posts.

## Result (FORUM OPINION)
- **Directory: "Victor: HP_Legend (Judge Decision 2:0)"** (May 27 – Jul 17, 2020; judged in 2021).
- **AncientPower (P45, May 8, 2021), vote HP:** "HP managed to convincingly argue Starkiller's exhaustion, the fact Resurrection pits ANH Vader as opposed to ROTJ Vader as well as the point regarding Starkiller withstanding the Emperor's power better than any other point raised here. Thus he managed to argue the structural integrity of his scaling chain better than Meatpants. Thus, despite how impressively Meatpants managed to argue his points. I cast my favor towards HP."
- **Cheth (P46, Sept 7, 2021), vote HP:** "I can't say I'm convinced Starkiller was operating at peak performance against Vader. I also was not convinced that Ressurection uses ROTJ Vader, which undermines Meatpants' main scaling chain. When speaking of the Palpatine fight, I find myself more on edge, but would still favour HP. While Jinn > Vader still stands to some degree, I don't see any clear connection to SK in which Jinn comes out favourable."
  - Cheth refers to "LadyKulvax"; this appears to be AncientPower's later name (UNCLEAR).
- **Side drama:**
  - ISV ("Vader's Legacy"/"The Fallen Warrior") interjected repeatedly: P21 "One quote renders all of this moot, one fucking quote."; P31 "You are both clowns…"; P32/P34 were 58k-character quote-and-image posts.
  - ISV accused MP of forging a quote. Azronger (P36): "Meatpants did not forge the quote." HP located it: "page 97 of the Wii Prima Guide" (the multiplayer skins / DS Galen bio section). ISV retracted (P40).

## Qui-Gon (MP)
### P6 "THE OLD RASCAL"
- Opens with: "Maul was pleased by this. Yet he could not find an opening for a final blow. The Jedi was too good."
- In TFU2, Starkiller couldn't gain an edge on Vader until he exploited the chest-panel wound Juno had inflicted.
- Vader grows from TFU2 to ESB/RotJ. Insider #62: "greater mastery over himself and over the Force", "largely freed himself of pain", "advanced his lightsaber technique", "a far more formidable foe on Bespin".
- George Lucas and Insider #70: PT Jedi "full flower". Jinn is faster and more agile than Vader and Kenobi (YouTube: RIefj6dOhnM, liEtSzWZPFo).
- Dynasty of Evil: "few duels lasted more than a minute."

### P17, P27
- **P17:** Starkiller's inconsistencies (exhaustion).
- **P27 sections:** "THE RETURN OF THE STRAW-MAN" (with Scarecrow images, which BoD and DC77 found unfunny).
  - "Exhausted and off-balance"
  - "Obi-Wan never saw Qui-Gon fight harder than this"
  - "Exhausted Qui-Gon with a few minutes respite > fresh Qui-Gon on Tatooine"
  - "Oneness"
- **Chain:** **"Maul > Jinn > Vader >> TFU2 Vader ~ Starkiller."**
- MP leaned on the Resurrection comic (Maul vs Vader) as RotJ Vader.
- P42: "I left out two quotes that outright debunk Starkiller being able to replicate most of his environmental feats on any given day."

## Starkiller (HP)
### P13
- Opens with "You were weak when I found you… your hatred has become your strength".
- **Sections:**
  1. Starkiller
  2. Vader
  3. Maul
  4. Conclusion
- **Exhaustion:** before facing Vader, Starkiller "(A) atomised The Salvation, and (B) pulverised an army of Starkiller Clones". (A) "took basically all that Starkiller had ('all the power of the Force')", and afterward he struggled to stand (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhOMe5NPfeI&t=0m41s).
- TFU2 novel: Vader's "power over the apprentice, however, was gone… The Force wrenched him into the air".
- **Resurrection:** "explicitly stated to be 'the answer' to the fan debate". It pits ANH Vader, not RotJ Vader, against Maul, and Vader "competes much more closely with Maul than… against Starkiller".
- Wrath of Darth Maul: "Having expected a greater challenge from Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan, he felt even more disgusted by them."
- Gillard levels: Jinn is a 7.
- **Conclusion:** "Galen’s vast superiority to Vader (and fight with Sidious) indicates he is a significantly better combatant than Darth Maul who is considerably better than Jinn. Tl;dr Galen >> Maul >> Jinn."

### P19 "Shall We?" and P43 "The Finale"
- Exhaustion, full power, inconsistencies.
- Starkiller vs the Emperor: the Emperor "wasn’t going all-out".
- P43 opens with the TPM script: "The SITH makes a quick move, bashes his lightsaber handle into QUI-GON's chin, and runs him through."
- "none of my argument is contingent on a sizeable gap between Maul and Jinn".

## Neutral assessment
- The judges decided on structure: Starkiller's exhaustion explains TFU2 parity with Vader, and Resurrection's Vader is ANH Vader. That broke MP's "Jinn > Vader ~ Starkiller" link.
- MP's PT-supremacy (Lucas/Insider) argument was respected but didn't connect to Starkiller.

**Q32** — Source: Valkpants
> In TFU2, Starkiller and Darth Vader engage in a lightsaber duel. Starkiller is unable to win until he tricks Vader by taking advantage of a wound inflicted by Juno on Vader’s chest panel. There had to be a way to free himself and avenge Juno at the same time... but a stalemate seemed unavoidable." The combatants fight in a prolonged lightsaber duel, and neither demonstrate clear superiority over the other - in fact a stalemate seemed likely. Although Galen has some incredible telekinetic feats, he isn’t able to manifest such feats combatively, or on a consistent basis. So, even if Darth Vader is incapable of matching some of these feats, such as pulling down an ISD, atomising the Salvation, or his one-off against the Emperor, this doesn’t matter because Starkiller has proven that he’s incapable of consistency in these showings. In a one-on-one duel, he is stalemated by Vader, thus it is logical to conclude that Darth Vader and Starkiller are both within the same ballpark combatively.
